reading.title: Big Ideas That Guide a Community
reading.purpose: Explore ten important civic words that describe rights, duties, and fair communities.
paras: Strong towns do not happen by luck. They grow when folks share clear rules about how to treat each other and care for their shared home.

Many towns prize freedom, the right to speak, think, and choose safely. With rights comes responsibility, a job you must carry out, like keeping parks clean or obeying road signs. Good citizenship means taking part in both your rights and your jobs in a town.

Fair play sits at the heart of town life. Justice means fair rules and fair acts for all. Equality means each person has the same rights and shots. Then each child gets an opportunity, a real chance to learn and help.

Good acts matter as much as laws. Folks show honor when they tell the truth and do right even when no one looks. Leaders gain wisdom, sound choice built from listening and learning. Folks show loyalty by standing firm by their town. Many show patriotism, a true love for their land, by helping make it great.
Even young kids live these big ideas each day at school and on their block.

choices: keeping neighborhood parks clean and following signs
every person having the same rights and chances
good judgment built from listening and learning
a steady love for a country shown by volunteering
qs.why: Paragraph 3 states that equality means "every person has the same rights and chances."

qs.q: Which sentence explains how folks show honor?
choices: Good acts matter as much as laws.
Folks show honor when they tell the truth and do right even when no one looks.
Leaders gain wisdom, sound choice built from listening and learning.
Even young kids live these big ideas each day at school and on their block.
qs.why: This sentence explains that honor means telling the truth and doing right even when no one looks.

ev.text: Folks show honor when they tell the truth and do right even when no one looks.

qs.q: According to the reading, why does freedom go hand in hand with responsibility?
choices: Good citizenship includes both rights and jobs.
Folks can only speak freely after they clean up a town park.
Road signs are the only rules that protect fair play in a town.
Young kids do not have any jobs to do until they grow up.
qs.why: Paragraph 2 explains that with rights comes responsibility, and good citizenship means taking part in both.

qs.q: What is the main idea of this reading?
choices: Only elected town leaders can show wisdom, loyalty, and justice in public life.
Shared values like freedom, fairness, and honor build strong towns.
Helping to clean a park is the single best way to practice good citizenship.
Laws are far more important than good acts in any neighborhood or school.
qs.why: The reading defines ten civic values and explains how living them together strengthens a town.
